instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the upper third. Grate the Gruyere, which should be about 1 1/2 cups.
Slice the zucchini into rounds about 1/8 inch thick.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the zucchini in one layer with 1/4 tsp salt. Cook for 2 minutes on each side, until soft and just starting to color. Transfer them to a plate. Repeat with the other 1 tbsp oil, the rest of the zucchini and 1/4 tsp salt.
In a bowl, whisk the cream, eggs, nutmeg, pepper and 1/2 tsp of the salt until smooth. Stir in half the cheese.
Overlap the zucchini slices in an 8 by 11 inch baking dish, in slightly slanting rows.
Pour the cream mixture over the zucchini and sprinkle on the rest of the cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes, until the custard is set in the middle and bubbling at the edges. Switch the oven to broil and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the top is golden. Watch it the whole time.
Leave it for 5 minutes, then cut into squares.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: No version had 20 ratings, so the lead is the highest-rated one that gave amounts: Frugal Flexitarian (5.0 from 5 ratings). The sources agree on thin zucchini slices, an egg and cream custard with nutmeg and Gruyere or Emmental, and a hot oven. They differ on how the zucchini is dried: Frugal Flexitarian fries the slices, France Today boils them for a couple of minutes, and Nigella softens them with shallot. This follows the frying, and the cream, egg and cheese amounts are scaled from Frugal's 2-zucchini version to a dinner for 4. Honest time is a few minutes over 45, because the zucchini cooks in two batches.
